onboarding.welcomeText: Priroda65 is a map of places the locals know: where pink salmon bite, where lingonberries grow, where to pitch a tent and where it's better not to go.
onboarding.welcomePoint2: No sign-up, no personal data collected
onboarding.welcomePoint3: Mark your own spot — and help others
onboarding.offlineTitle: The map works where there's no signal
onboarding.offlineText: In the taiga, on the coast and in the mountains there is often no internet. Download the Sakhalin map once over Wi-Fi — it will open anywhere, and GPS will show where you are using satellites.
onboarding.legalTitle: A few important words before you go
onboarding.legal1: Priroda65 is an information service. Spots are added by users; we review them but cannot guarantee their accuracy.
onboarding.legal2: The developers are not responsible for fines for poaching or breaking fishing and hunting rules, for entering restricted military or border zones, or for accidents in nature.
onboarding.legal3: Before fishing, hunting or foraging, check the current seasons and rules with Rosrybolovstvo (the Federal Fisheries Agency), nature reserve administrations and local authorities.
onboarding.legal4: Part of the coast is in the border zone — you may need a permit to visit it.
info.title: Sakhalin travel guide
info.lead: Sakhalin is taiga, mountains, hundreds of rivers and a cold sea. The fishing is excellent and the berry patches are generous, but the island's nature demands preparation. Here's what you should know before heading out.
info.safetyTitle: Safety in the forest and mountains
info.zonesTitle: Nature reserves and the border zone
info.bearsText: Sakhalin has many brown bears, especially near rivers during the salmon run. Walk noisily and in a group, don't leave food or waste around camp, and keep away from fish carcasses on the riverbank. If you see a bear, don't run and don't approach — back away calmly without turning your back on it.
info.ticksText: From spring to midsummer, ticks are active in grass and undergrowth. Wear closed, light-coloured clothing, use repellent and check yourself every couple of hours. An attached tick should be removed and a doctor seen as soon as possible.
info.weatherText: The weather on the island can change within an hour: fog, wind and rain roll in from the sea. Bring warm waterproof clothing even in summer, and check the forecast and storm warnings before heading into the mountains or along the coast.
info.riversText: After rain, mountain rivers rise quickly and the water is cold. Don't wade across a fast-flowing stream. On the coast, watch the tide: some stretches of shore under the cliffs get cut off by the water.
info.plan1: Tell someone close your route and when you plan to be back.
info.plan2: Download the offline map, charge your phone and bring a power bank.
info.plan3: Take water, extra food, a first-aid kit, a knife, matches and a flashlight.
info.fishingText1: Sakhalin is famous for salmon — pink salmon, chum and coho — as well as char and white-spotted char. Seasons, permitted gear and catch limits are set by the Fishing Rules for the Far Eastern fishery basin, and during the salmon run extra restrictions often apply on spawning rivers.
info.fishingText2: The rules change every season. Before fishing, check the current restrictions on the website of the Sakhalin-Kuril Territorial Administration of Rosrybolovstvo. Spots in Priroda65 show where people fish, but they don't override the rules.
info.gatheringText1: In late summer and autumn, people on the island pick lingonberries, blueberries, cloudberries, honeysuckle and other berries, and the forests are full of mushrooms. Timing depends on the year and the area, so check the latest community spots.
info.gatheringText2: Don't pick mushrooms or berries you don't know. Picking may be prohibited in specially protected natural areas — check the rules in advance.
info.zonesText1: Sakhalin has the Poronaysky Nature Reserve, wildlife sanctuaries and natural monuments. Each has its own visiting rules: some require a permit, some prohibit fishing, hunting and foraging.
info.zonesText2: Part of the coast is in the border zone, and you may need a permit to visit it. There are also restricted military sites. Check boundaries and rules with local authorities before your trip.
info.emergencyText: Call 112 — the single emergency number. It works with a zero balance and without a SIM card. Tell the dispatcher your coordinates: the app's SOS screen shows them in large print, even offline.
info.app1: Download the offline map over Wi-Fi — the "Offline map" button on the map.
info.app2: Tap a spot to see its description, build a route or share it.
info.app3: The crosshair button shows where you are via GPS satellites. The grid helps estimate distance: one cell is 100 metres.
info.app4: Know a good spot? Tap "Mark a spot" — once reviewed, everyone will see it.
info.faq1q: Do I need to sign up for Priroda65?
info.faq1a: No. You can use the map and all its features without signing up, and we don't collect personal data.
info.faq2a: Yes. Download the Sakhalin map with the "Offline map" button while you have Wi-Fi. After that, the map, spots and GPS work without a connection.
info.faq3q: How do I add my own spot to the map?
info.faq3a: Tap "Mark a spot", choose a point on the map and fill in a short form. The spot will appear after a moderator reviews it.
info.faq4q: Why isn't my spot on the map yet?
info.faq4a: A moderator reviews every submission so that spam, mistakes and prohibited places don't end up on the map. This usually takes up to a day.
info.disclaimer: Priroda65 is an information service. The developers are not responsible for fines for breaking fishing and hunting rules, entering restricted zones, or accidents in nature. Check the current rules with Rosrybolovstvo, nature reserve administrations and local authorities.
